title: FBI National Crime Information Center apparently breached, CNN and NBC report
date_note: Date of the CNN report as relayed by Arab News (published 21 November, says CNN reported on Friday); the date of the intrusion is not stated.
place: Washington, DC, United States (FBI headquarters; location of the system not stated)
summary: CNN, relayed by Arab News, and NBC News reported on Friday an apparent breach of the FBI National Crime Information Center, the second in recent months. On Saturday AP, citing a person familiar with the matter, said the FBI is investigating an apparent hack; the FBI declined to comment. ABC News says a law enforcement source confirmed the database was hacked. Trump said "it's not good"; ABC says the perpetrators and scale are unclear.
plain: News outlets report a hack of the FBI's national criminal database; a law enforcement source told ABC News it was hacked. The FBI has not commented, and who did it and the scale are unclear.
exec: A reported hack of a core US law-enforcement database; the FBI has not commented and the scale is unclear.

sources.name: NBC News (Ryan J. Reilly, Colleen Long, Kyla Guilfoil)
ABC News (Nicholas Kerr, Luke Barr), via ABC7 New York

validation.note: CNN (relayed by Arab News and CNN Brasil), NBC News, AP (via KSL) and ABC News (via ABC7) each cite their own anonymous sources; ABC says a law enforcement source confirmed the hack. The FBI declined to comment to AP and did not respond to ABC; no FBI or DOJ statement read, so status stays developing. Trump's quoted words (AP, ABC) are "it's not good"; EFE (ABC Color) calls his remarks a confirmation. CNN original answered 451.

review.note: Compared title, date, 'second breach', two people briefed, FBI no comment as of Friday night (NBC, Arab News, CNN Brasil), Trump Fox News quote (Infobae, EFE) with sources; developing status fits
